entries.german:
Karl IV. tauscht, nachdem er Achalm und Hohenstaufen mit Gewalt wieder ans Reich gebracht, mit Rat und Willen der Kurfürsten als König von Böhmen mit dem Reich dergestalt, dass dieses die jenen beiden Vesten näher gelegenen, seinerseits von den Grafen Ludwig und Ludwig von Oettingen mit böhmischen Krongeldern erkauften Vesten Lauterburg und Rosenstein und die Städte Alen und Heubach erhält, und dagegen an Böhmen die Vesten Parkstein und Karlswald nebst der Stadt zu der Weiden abtritt.(in lat.).

Zeugen: venerabiles Marquardus Augustensis, Johannes Olomucensis, Johannes Luthomuschlensis, imperialis aule cancellarius, Theodricus Mindensis et Bertoldus Eystetensis ecclesiarum episcopi, illustres Rupertus iunior comes palatinus Reni, Bavarie, Redacherus Braunswicensis, Przimislaus Teschinensis et Johannes Opavie duces, spectabiles Burghardus, imperialis curie magister, Magdeburgensis et Friedricus Nurembergensis burggravii, Eberhardus Wirtembergensis, Ulricus senior de Helfenstein, advocatus Swevie, Henricus de Montfort, Ludowicus senior et Ludowicus iunior de Otingen comites, Ulricus et Johannes lantgravii Leutembergenses ac nobiles Gerlacus de Hohenloch, Czenko de Lipa, summus regni Boemie marescallus et camerarius, Wilhelmus de Rechperg, Friedericus de Heydeck, Sbinco de Hazemburg, spuremus magister, Haschco de Swereticz et Thimo de Koldicz, magistri imperialis camere, Ogerius de Landstein et Johannes de Rosemberg et alii quamplures nostri et imperii sacri principes, nobiles et fideles
entries.english:
After recovering Achalm and Hohenstaufen for the Empire by force, Karl IV, with the counsel and consent of the electors, makes an exchange between the Kingdom of Bohemia and the Empire: the Empire is to receive the fortresses Lauterburg and Rosenstein, nearer to the two aforementioned castles and purchased by the Counts Ludwig and Ludwig von Oettingen with Bohemian crown funds, as well as the towns of Alen and Heubach; in exchange Bohemia receives the fortresses Parkstein and Karlswald and the town of Weiden. (In Latin.)

Witnesses: the venerable Marquardus of Augsburg, Johannes of Olomouc, Johannes of Leitomischl, chancellor of the imperial court, Theodricus of Minden, and Bertoldus of Eichstätt, bishops; the illustrious Rupertus iunior, Count Palatine of the Rhine and Duke of Bavaria, Redacherus of Brunswick, Przimislaus of Teschen, and Johannes of Opava, dukes; the distinguished Burghardus, steward of the imperial court and Burgrave of Magdeburg, and Friedricus, Burgrave of Nuremberg; Eberhardus of Wirtemberg, Ulricus senior of Helfenstein, advocate of Swabia, Henricus of Montfort, Ludowicus senior and Ludowicus iunior of Oettingen, counts; Ulricus and Johannes, landgraves of Leuchtenberg; and the nobles Gerlacus of Hohenlohe, Czenko of Lipa, chief marshal and chamberlain of the Kingdom of Bohemia, Wilhelmus of Rechperg, Friedericus of Heydeck, Sbinco of Hazemburg, chief chamberlain, Haschco of Swereticz and Thimo of Koldicz, imperial chamberlains, Ogerius of Landstein, and Johannes of Rosemberg; and many other princes, nobles, and faithful men of ours and of the Holy Empire.
